title: No leader: any node coordinates, the partition key picks 3 replicas
caption: hash(partition key) gives a token on the ring; the next RF = 3 nodes clockwise own that partition.

steps.text: The client driver sends the request to any node; that node acts as coordinator for this request only. There is no primary to fail over.
The coordinator hashes the partition key (conversation_id = c1) to a token and finds the 3 nodes that own it on the ring.
It forwards to all 3 replicas in parallel and waits for as many as the consistency level asks for (1, 2 = QUORUM, or 3 = ALL).
Every row of partition c1 lives on exactly these 3 nodes. Adding nodes moves token ranges, not individual rows.

scenarios.name: A replica is down
scenarios.summary: No leader means no failover: with RF = 3 a QUORUM request still succeeds on the two live replicas, and the coordinator keeps a hint for the third.

steps.text: The client sends a request for c1 to any node; it coordinates.
Replica 3 has crashed. Its share of c1 can't be written or read right now.
Replicas 1 and 2 answer: 2 of 3 is a quorum, so the request succeeds without any election or promotion.
If the coordinator itself dies, the driver just retries on another node: every node can coordinate.

scenarios.name: Risk: huge partition
scenarios.summary: A partition lives on exactly RF nodes, so one unbounded partition (a huge chat, a busy sensor) overloads 3 nodes however big the cluster is.

steps.text: A single conversation gets millions of messages, all under the same partition key c1.
Every write and read for it lands on the same 3 replicas; they grow to many GB for one partition and slow down on compaction and repair.
Adding nodes doesn't help: the token of c1 still maps to 3 owners.
Mitigation: bucket the key, e.g. (conversation_id, day), so each partition stays bounded (aim for well under 100 MB) and buckets spread over the ring.

scenarios.name: Alternative: leader
scenarios.summary: A leader per shard (MongoDB, Postgres): simple, strongly consistent writes, but writes stop for that shard until a new leader is elected.

steps.text: Writes for this shard must go to its one leader.
The leader orders every write and replicates it: no conflicts, no last-write-wins.
The leader dies: writes for this shard fail until the followers elect a new one (seconds).
